purpose: Credit formal sources separately from mathematical literature provenance and from resource accounting.
default_rule: A project-local declaration in the checked-in formalization dependency inventory is credited as formalized in this project unless an explicit positive external-formalization claim applies to that exact declaration.
ordinary_library_rule: Declarations outside the project-local inventory, including ordinary Mathlib/Lean dependencies, are upstream library dependencies and are not counted as project formalizations.
resource_rule: Project-formalization credit means the current Lean artifact was produced or independently rederived in this project and belongs to the formalization campaign; it does not assert that every token or edit was machine-generated. Adapted/copied artifacts can also incur project adaptation cost while retaining upstream formal credit.
positive_claim_rule: Only explicit source-side provenance evidence creates a non-default formal-provenance relation. Absence of a positive external formal-provenance citation is treated as project formalization under the project's citation discipline.

primary_categories.project_native: No positive external formal-provenance claim applies; formalization credit is local to this project.
primary_categories.project_with_formal_reference: The source explicitly credits an external formal development for theorem selection, comparison, historical ancestry, or a donor strategy, while stating that the current definition/proof is independently developed or replaced locally.
primary_categories.adapted_or_ported: The current Lean artifact materially adapts, ports, generalizes, or wraps a formal construction/result credited to an external formal source.
primary_categories.copied_or_rehomed: The current Lean artifact is copied or essentially verbatim from an external formal source, possibly with namespace/module-system changes.
